item.title: Labasa stamp early authority
item.description: Defending 2026 Extra Battle of the Giants champions Labasa FC stamped their authority on day one of the tournament after edging Nasinu FC 1-0 at the 4R Stadium at Govind Park in Ba yesterday. The Babasiga Lions struck in the first half through Joseph Joe and held on firmly in the second half to secure all three points.
item.content:encoded:
Defending 2026 Extra Battle of the Giants champions Labasa FC stamped their authority on day one of the tournament after edging Nasinu FC 1-0 at the 4R Stadium at Govind Park in Ba yesterday.

The Babasiga Lions struck in the first half through Joseph Joe and held on firmly in the second half to secure all three points.

Labasa created several opportunities to extend its lead, but Nasinu’s young side showed determination and resilience to keep the defending champions at bay.

Labasa head coach Alvin Chand was satisfied with the result, admitting that defending the title away from home would be a tough challenge.

“We won in Labasa last year and this year we are here in Ba. It will be tough to defend, but we are looking forward to it.

“I thank my boys. We managed to get the three points. The first game is always tough in tournaments and the result can go either way, but we managed to get the win,” Chand said.

Nasinu head coach Abunesh Kapur was proud of his young players despite the narrow defeat.

“It was unfortunate, but I’m proud of my team. We have a young team, and six of them are U20 players,” Kapur said.

item.title: Houshmand and Brooks Fiji Pro champions
item.description: FIJI Pro 2026 champions Cole Houshmand and Erin Brooks stamped their authority on the World Surf League’s Pacific Leg, claiming memorable victories after a spectacular Finals Day at Cloudbreak on Tavarua Island yesterday. Cloudbreak saved some of its finest conditions for the final day, providing a fitting stage for two surfers in outstanding form to celebrate major victories and strengthen their
item.content:encoded:
FIJI Pro 2026 champions Cole Houshmand and Erin Brooks stamped their authority on the World Surf League’s Pacific Leg, claiming memorable victories after a spectacular Finals Day at Cloudbreak on Tavarua Island yesterday.

Cloudbreak saved some of its finest conditions for the final day, providing a fitting stage for two surfers in outstanding form to celebrate major victories and strengthen their positions heading into the final stretch of the Championship Tour season.

For Canadian star Brooks, the victory completed a remarkable Pacific Leg sweep and secured her second Fiji Pro title. Her triumph came after another impressive run at Cloudbreak, although the anticipated Final showdown with friend Isabella Nichols was denied after Nichols suffered an unfortunate injury during her semifinal.

Brooks’ success has lifted her to No.8 in the rankings as the Championship Tour now moves to Lower Trestles in Southern California. With valuable points still available, she remains firmly in contention to make a stronger push in the World Title race.

On the men’s side, American Cole Houshmand continued his extraordinary rise, claiming his third Championship Tour victory from three Final appearances.

The Fiji triumph added to his victories at Bells Beach and Brazil, further establishing Houshmand as one of the sport’s most dangerous competitors.

His Finals Day performance was nothing short of spectacular.

Houshmand produced a 9.43-point ride in the semifinals before delivering another outstanding performance in the Final against two-time Fiji Pro winner Gabriel Medina.

item.title: NEW talent adds strength to FLYING FIJIANS
item.description: FIJI Water Flying Fijians captain Tevita Ikanivere believes the team is building the right foundation ahead of the Pacific Nations Cup (PNC) with hard work and new talent helping strengthen the squad. The flying Fijians have gone through several demanding training sessions in preparation for the upcoming PNC, and Ikanivere said hard work has helped bring the players closer together.
item.content:encoded:
FIJI Water Flying Fijians captain Tevita Ikanivere believes the team is building the right foundation ahead of the Pacific Nations Cup (PNC) with hard work and new talent helping strengthen the squad.

The flying Fijians have gone through several demanding training sessions in preparation for the upcoming PNC, and Ikanivere said hard work has helped bring the players closer together.

“The boys have gotten to know each other pretty well after a few sessions,” Ikanivere said.

“I think that’s the best way to bring the team together. That’s what we’ve been doing for the past few days.”

Ikanivere said there was a clear message across the squad, from management and the coaching staff to the players as they look to build towards their next challenge.

“The team has been strengthened in connection.”

All message around that, from management down the players, even to the coach is the same.

“We just want to build and make sure we’re ready when we get to the next.”

The captain is also encouraged by the opportunity to work with emerging players, including Fijian Drua development squad member, 19-year-old Maleli Nauvasi.

Ikanivere said Nauvasi had already spent two years in the Drua environment and had continued to develop before earning his opportunity with the flying Fijians squad.

“He’s grown and he’s played very well for the training this year and for the development. I think it’s a well-deserved one for him,” he said.

Ikanivere also welcomed Terio Tamani, who was previously part of the Fiji Airways sevens squad, saying he brought something different to the team. Having played alongside Tamani for Suva, Ikanivere said he had enjoyed seeing the former sevens player bring his experience and professionalism into the squad.

“He brings something new to this team. Even I get to learn from him, watch him train,” Ikanivere said.

The captain believes the movement of players through Fiji’s different rugby pathways is important for the growth of the sport.

“It’s good for the future. It’s good for Fiji Rugby, for the Flying Fijians, to be able to bring in new talent, he said.

Ikanivere said the professionalism being developed across the various teams and pathways would ultimately strengthen Fiji Rugby.

item.title: U17 Fiji girls squad named ahead of Cairns
item.description: TWENTY players have been selected to represent Fiji at the Australian Football League (AFL) Pacific Nations challenge in Cairns Australia. AFL Fiji has named a 20-member Fiji under-17 girls squad for the Pacific Nations Challenge in Cairns, Queensland, Australia.
item.content:encoded:
TWENTY players have been selected to represent Fiji at the Australian Football League (AFL) Pacific Nations challenge in Cairns Australia.

AFL Fiji has named a 20-member Fiji under-17 girls squad for the Pacific Nations Challenge in Cairns, Queensland, Australia.

The young players will have the opportunity to represent Fiji on the international stage as they compete against teams at the regional tournament.

The squad features a mix of young talent across various local schools, with the players selected to carry Fiji’s hopes in the U17 girls competition. The 20-member squad are; Adi Ema Vuicuvu, Tabitha Salusalu, Elenoa Ratusaki, Inise Masi, Suliana Daunia, Ruby Kulinidilo, Wasela Saurara, Katarina Natoga, Paulina Collin, Lice Baleisuva, Jackie Naicegu, Sesilia Waibuta, Serai Vosataki, Lynn Catinaivalu, Sera Naisualevu, Lucinda Bulatiko, Kinishasa Sawake, Janviv Salailagi, Elina Wati and Venina Naisaluwaki.

The tournament in Cairns will provide Fiji U17 girls with valuable international exposure and an opportunity to test themselves against teams from the region.

The squad will now turn its attention to preparations for the challenge ahead, with the players aiming to make the most of their opportunity to represent Fiji.

The AFL Pacific Nations Challenge will take place on September 11-13 at Cairns, Queensland, Australia.

item.title: Police wives wrap up annual tournament
item.description: THE 2026 Fiji Police Wives Association Annual Tournament concluded yesterday at the National Netball Centre with organisers reflecting on two days of competition that brought together police families while strengthening the association’s welfare role. With 46 teams representing the seven divisions of the Fiji Police Force, the tournament provided more than an opportunity for members to compete, wi
item.content:encoded:
THE 2026 Fiji Police Wives Association Annual Tournament concluded yesterday at the National Netball Centre with organisers reflecting on two days of competition that brought together police families while strengthening the association’s welfare role.

With 46 teams representing the seven divisions of the Fiji Police Force, the tournament provided more than an opportunity for members to compete, with the association using the event to encourage unity, strengthen relationships and support families.

Fiji Police Wives Association president Iva Driu said the tournament had achieved its purpose of bringing members together.

“This year is quite fantastic, working together. The reason for the game here is to unite us and strengthen us to play a role in supporting our families,” Driu said.

She said the strong turnout demonstrated the support members continued to have for the association and its activities.

“It shows the support for the association, and we are always looking forward to the event for the families to come together and unite and strengthen our relationship,” she said.

Driu said this year’s tournament also introduced changes aimed at making the event more inclusive, including the involvement of children and the introduction of handicaps.

The participation of younger wives was another positive development, with junior members joining teams and bringing a new generation into the association’s annual event.

“In the past years, we, older ladies, older wives, used to be part of the team. But now, young wives, they are juniors, and they are part of the team this year,” Driu said.

She said the tournament also provided the association with an opportunity to generate income, which could contribute towards its activities and welfare initiatives.

Looking beyond this year’s event, Driu said the association wanted to expand its support to families who were unable to attend its tournaments.

“We are looking forward to some development in our association, and we are planning to have some tournaments that can assist some families who are not fortunate enough to come to the events,” she said.

She said the association hoped future activities could reach families directly and provide assistance where it was needed.

Driu also thanked the association’s patrons and the division wives who helped share information and coordinate participation across the seven divisions.

Their contribution, she said, was vital to the successful staging of the event.

For the association, the conclusion of the tournament marks the beginning of preparations for future initiatives, with a focus on growing participation while strengthening its welfare support for police families.

item.title: Suva target small gains in round 6
item.description: THE FMF Suva women’s rugby captain Elenoa Matanisiga believes small improvements in their game will be important as they prepare for the next round of the Subrails Marama Cup Championship. Matanisiga said the team did not need to make changes but would focus on areas that could improve their performance in their next match.
item.content:encoded:
THE FMF Suva women’s rugby captain Elenoa Matanisiga believes small improvements in their game will be important as they prepare for the next round of the Subrails Marama Cup Championship.

Matanisiga said the team did not need to make changes but would focus on areas that could improve their performance in their next match.

“We just need to do alot of small workouts, and I feel like we need to work on our support plays, our forwards and the scrums,” Matanisiga said.

Suva currently sits in third place of the Subrails Marama Cup points table, a few points behind Namosi who is in first place and Nadi at second place.

She said the team was otherwise in good shape and would use the lead-up to Round 6 to sharpen their execution.

“Other than that, we’re all good,” she said.

For Suva, the focus will be on making sure the work done during training translates into better support and consistency when they return to the field.

Round 6 of the Subrails Marama Cup championship fixtures, Suva will take on Kadavu at 1pm at the Suva Grammar School grounds, while Lautoka hosts points table leader Namosi at 11am at Churchill Park in Lautoka. Also at 11am, Naitasiri faces Macuata at Ratu Cakobau Park in Nausori, Nadi plays Nasinu at Prince Charles Park in Nadi, while Tailevu meets Rewa at the Nakelo District School ground and Nadroga takes on Ba at 11am at Lawaqa Park in Sigatoka.

The Subrails Marama Cup Championship continues with Round 6 fixtures today, with teams looking to strengthen their positions as the competition progresses.

item.title: Fiji Pearls ready for Tonga challenge
item.description: The release of the Oceania Netball World Cup Qualifiers draw has given Crest Fiji Pearls head coach Michelle Parsons greater clarity as the team enters the final stages of preparation for the tournament in Tonga. Fiji will open its campaign against the Cook Islands on September 15, with the draw now allowing Parsons and her coaching team to fine-tune their preparations and match-day plans.
item.content:encoded:
The release of the Oceania Netball World Cup Qualifiers draw has given Crest Fiji Pearls head coach Michelle Parsons greater clarity as the team enters the final stages of preparation for the tournament in Tonga.

Fiji will open its campaign against the Cook Islands on September 15, with the draw now allowing Parsons and her coaching team to fine-tune their preparations and match-day plans.

Parsons said her initial reaction to the draw was one of relief, as the schedule provided certainty around the team’s planning.

“My first reaction to the release of the draw was more around the ability to now plan and prepare our schedule and timings,” Parsons said.

“It’s always good to know who we are playing and when, so you feel settled with what is happening.”

Parsons highlights that knowing our’ first opponent would also help shape their preparation, with the team now able to study the Cook Islands and identify areas that could influence their approach.

“Knowing your first opponent does help you prepare. You look at any opposition knowledge you have that may help with your own preparation,” she said.

Parsons also spoke highly of the Cook Islands’ rich netball history and the legacy of players who have represented the nation at the international level.

“The recent passing of Ana Noovao hit the netball communities across the world and we mourned the loss of such a beautiful wahine alongside our Cook Island whānau,” Parsons said.

While respecting the Cook Islands’ history, Parsons is also well aware of the quality Fiji will face when the two sides meet in Tonga.

She said the Cook Islands squad brings together a combination of experience and emerging talent, making them a side Fiji cannot afford to underestimate.

For the Crest Fiji Pearls, the September 15 clash will be the first step in what is expected to be a highly competitive Oceania qualifying campaign, with the ultimate prize being qualification for the 2027 Netball World Cup in Sydney.

With the draw now confirmed, the countdown has moved another step closer to match day and Parsons believes having clarity around the schedule will allow the Pearls to focus on what matters most: preparing to perform when they take the court in Tonga.

The Oceania qualifiers will be held in Tonga from September 14–18, with Fiji opening its campaign against the Cook Islands on September 15.
